The finished front cover visibly includes all four prescribed lines with their exact wording and capitalization. Typography leads the composition, and the cover has the prescribed 4:5 page proportion. Line wrapping, placement and typographic treatment may vary; missing, altered or unreadable wording fails.

Apply to delivered opener, narrative and study spreads, comparing photographs directly with the corresponding supplied P01.jpg–P10.jpg references. Assignments are opener-work: P01; opener-provisions: P03; opener-together: P06; narrative-work: P01, P02, P09; narrative-provisions: P03, P04, P05; narrative-together: P06, P07, P08, P10; narrative-closing: P01, P04, P10; each study-pNN: its matching PNN photograph. Each assigned source must have at least one complete, unobscured scene in that individual artwork. Scaling and placement may vary, but replacement imagery, missing sources, cropping every occurrence, colorization, mirroring, rotation, distortion or changes to depicted contents fail. This requirement does not assign a photograph to the cover.

For every photograph on each opener, narrative or individual study spread, read its associated caption and compare all five fields with its record in 01-client-facts.en.md. Require the correct P-number, neutral caption label, recorded place, month/year and full credit. The dates are June 1942 for P01, P05, P06 and P07; August 1942 for P02, P03 and P04; July 1942 for P08; November 1942 for P09 and P10. P07 and P08 retain Anacostia, D.C.; Frederick Douglass housing project as their recorded place; the other records use Washington, D.C. Caption placement and field order may vary, and one clearly applicable credit may serve an entire spread. Missing fields, ambiguous image-to-caption associations, swapped records or altered record facts fail.

Apply to narrative-work, narrative-provisions, narrative-together, narrative-closing and every delivered study-p01–study-p10. Each must contain a distinct English editorial bridge of 30–50 words, counting the bridge separately from headings and captions. Assess statements against the chapter aims and photograph records in 01-client-facts.en.md. Work concerns the three separate labor settings; provisions connects separate store, shopping and home-meal records; togetherness connects distinct gatherings and occasions. The closing spread associates P01, P04 and P10 without inventing a shared event. Individual studies may discuss their single record in relation to their chapter without displaying another photograph. Reading order and original editorial phrasing may vary. Unsupported identities, relationships, chronology or settings fail, including treating P03 and P04 as one documented visit, P07 and P08 as one dated occasion, or assigning unrecorded left/right identities to P10.

If an opener or narrative spread includes a cropped supplementary photograph, the word Detail must visibly identify that crop. A spread without additional crops passes without printing this label. A label does not excuse omission of the required intact source appearance.

Visible authored publication headings, introductions, captions and editorial bridges are in English. Archival lettering within the original photographs is source content and is not evaluated as newly authored editorial text.

Each board contains both a cover study and a Work in view spread study using the supplied P01, P02 and P09 records. Across the boards, image prominence, caption-led reading and image pairing produce three visibly different sequencing approaches corresponding to their role names. Layout and type choices may differ substantially; cosmetic variations that do not demonstrate the three approaches, missing studies or substitutions for the common records fail.

The specification occupies one page and explicitly identifies one of the three proposed directions, explains its narrative rationale, and states page and spread ratios, a numeric grid column count, inner reading margin, type hierarchy, actual font names, required caption fields, all four exact cover lines and all three exact numbered chapter names. Ratios must be 4:5 and 8:5, and the margin must be at least 5% of page width on both gutter sides. Any column count and named font choices are allowed. Missing entries, contradictory geometry or generic font categories without actual names fail.

Read the specification to identify the chosen board, then compare the finished cover and spreads with that board's sequencing approach and editorial hierarchy. The final publication must recognizably develop that selection. Refinement and different arrangements for different photograph sets are allowed; an unresolved mixture of competing directions or a finished system unrelated to the documented selection fails.

Both documents contain the four prescribed cover lines and the three numbered chapter names without changed spelling or capitalization. In the presentation, entries may appear in readable reused artwork or in authored text. All seven must be recoverable; an omitted entry or a shortened replacement fails. Printed cover and opener wording is additionally assessed by the corresponding image checks and text constraints.

All seventeen spreads are flat and upright, with 4:5 pages forming 8:5 spreads and clear inner reading margins of at least 5% of page width on both sides of the gutter. Visible alignment follows the specified column count, and heading hierarchy, sample-sequence folios and caption treatment operate as one system consistent with the specification. Elements may span columns and layouts may vary, including individual studies. Contradictory grids, altered hierarchy, missing folios or inadequate reading margins fail.

The presentation explicitly repeats the specification's selected numeric column count, 4:5 page ratio, 8:5 spread ratio and inner margin of at least 5% of page width on each gutter side. Readable reuse of the specification can provide this evidence. Merely showing layouts without stating these facts, omitting a fact or contradicting the specification fails.

Each opener visibly prints its corresponding exact numbered chapter name and a short English introduction adapted from the chapter aim. Work frames separate forms of labor; provisions associates store, shopping and home-table settings; togetherness frames distinct occasions and forms of gathering. Original phrasing is allowed, with no prescribed numerical introduction length. Missing introductions, wrong chapter headings or invented continuity between records fail.

Review the complete 10-second video against the delivered artworks and presentation map. Require recognizable reuse of the finished cover and all seventeen finished spreads, retaining their page compositions and captions. The sequence follows the map and places studies P01, P02 and P09 in Work in view; P03, P04 and P05 in Daily provisions; and P06, P07, P08 and P10 in Being together. Ordering within each chapter and transition style may vary. Missing artworks, wrong chapter placement, disagreement with the map, obscured compositions or a different duration fail.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation contains at least 16 pages and explicitly names the specification's selected direction on page 1. More pages and flexible page organization are allowed. An insufficient page count, absent page-1 selection or a selection inconsistent with the specification fails.

The reading-order map identifies the cover and all seventeen spreads and gives each an unambiguous sequence position. It places study-p01, study-p02 and study-p09 within Work in view; study-p03, study-p04 and study-p05 within Daily provisions; and study-p06, study-p07, study-p08 and study-p10 within Being together. Ordering within a chapter is open. Missing entries, unclear sequence positions or studies assigned to the wrong chapter fail.

Find visible reuse of every listed source within the presentation: all three direction boards, the selected specification, the finished cover and all seventeen finished spreads. Scaling and grouping are allowed if each source remains recognizable and retains its substantive composition. Text-only mentions, replacement designs or omission of any source fail.

The finished core artworks develop the direction explicitly selected in the specification and share its editorial hierarchy. The core spreads follow the specified grid and matching heading, sample-folio and caption systems. The cover and core spreads use the required proportions, with at least 5% page-width reading clearance on both sides of each spread's gutter.

The six individual studies extend their Work in view or Daily provisions chapter's established grid, type hierarchy, folios and caption treatment. Each study remains an upright 8:5 facing-page spread with 4:5 pages and the prescribed inner reading margins.

The four individual studies extend the Being together chapter's established grid, type hierarchy, folios and caption treatment. Each study remains an upright 8:5 facing-page spread with 4:5 pages and the prescribed inner reading margins.
